description: Make the vendored check-agent-frontmatter smoke zero-dep so cam init no longer depends on Bun auto-install resolving js-yaml from a tmpdir.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Breaking change v4 to v5: js-yaml 5.x is ESM-only and the default export was REMOVED; only named exports (load, dump, etc.) are exposed. v4 still ships both. A code path using `import yaml from 'js-yaml'` works in v4 but throws `SyntaxError: Missing 'default' export` under v5. Named-import `import { load } from 'js-yaml'` is compatible with both v4 and v5.

When Bun runs a script in a directory with no package.json, no bun.lockb, and no node_modules, an unresolved bare-specifier import triggers auto-install of the package's `latest` tag from npm into a global cache. There is no `--no-install` flag. Determinism is only achieved when a lockfile, package.json with a pinned version, an inline version-specifier (e.g. `import foo from 'foo@4'`), or a local node_modules is present. A vendored script materialized to a bare tmpdir therefore has non-deterministic dependency resolution (depends on whichever version `latest` resolved at first auto-install, cached globally).

userStories.title: Make check-agent-frontmatter zero-dep (hand-rolled frontmatter parser)
userStories.description: As a cam-cli operator, I need `cam init` to never fail with `Missing 'default' export` because Bun auto-install resolved js-yaml@5 in a node_modules-less tmpdir, so the vendored smoke must parse frontmatter with zero runtime npm dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts no longer contains `import yaml from 'js-yaml'` (or any other bare-specifier import of js-yaml). [oracle: file-assert: ! grep -q "from 'js-yaml'" vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]

vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts has no bare-specifier import other than node: built-ins (so a tmpdir invocation cannot trigger Bun auto-install). The check explicitly rejects `from 'js-yaml'` while allowing `from 'node:fs'` etc. [oracle: file-assert: ! (grep -nE "^import .* from '[^/.]" vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts | grep -v "from 'node:")]
Preserved diagnostic: missing trailing LF. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q 'missing trailing LF' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: missing opening frontmatter delimiter. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q "missing opening '---' frontmatter delimiter" vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: missing closing frontmatter delimiter. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q "missing closing '---' frontmatter delimiter" vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: frontmatter must be a YAML mapping. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q 'frontmatter must be a YAML mapping' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: missing required key loop emits `missing required key '<key>'`. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q "missing required key '" vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: must declare at least one of tools/disallowedTools. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q 'must declare at least one of' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: name does not match filename slug. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q 'does not match filename slug' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: model must be a non-empty string. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q 'must be a non-empty string' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]
Preserved diagnostic: frontmatter has no body. [oracle: file-assert: grep -F -q 'frontmatter has no body' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]

Diagnostic format stays gcc-style `<file>:<line>: <reason>` and the closing-delimiter fallback line number for non-source-line violations is preserved. [oracle: file-assert: grep -q 'closeLine' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts && grep -q '\${d.file}:\${d.line}: \${d.reason}' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]

Exit-code contract is preserved: 0 ok, 1 violation, 2 environmental. [oracle: file-assert: grep -q 'process.exit(0)' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts && grep -q 'process.exit(1)' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts && grep -q 'process.exit(2)' vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts]

Malformed-YAML diagnostic still emits a line number; the hand-rolled parser surfaces the offending line via the same `+2` offset semantics (offset = line-within-frontmatter + 2 to convert to file-line) used for the old `mark.line + 2` calculation. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Embedded copy regenerated: `bun run embed-vendor` was run and the generated `src/vendor/_generated.ts` reflects the new vendor source byte-for-byte. [oracle: named-command: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Vendor drift check passes. [oracle: named-command: bun run embed-vendor:check]

Runtime correctness: the previously-failing init test `writes config.toml with permission_mode=bypassPermissions on a fresh path` now passes (this is the real correctness oracle, since vendor/ is excluded from typecheck). [oracle: named-command: bun test test/init.test.ts -t 'writes config.toml with permission_mode=bypassPermissions on a fresh path']

Runtime correctness: the previously-failing init test `preserves existing keys when re-running` now passes. [oracle: named-command: bun test test/init.test.ts -t 'preserves existing keys when re-running']
Typecheck passes (note: vendor/ is excluded from tsconfig — this gate only validates the rest of the tree is still green after any incidental edits). [oracle: named-command: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass. [oracle: named-command: bun test]

vendor/README.md row for `check-agent-frontmatter.ts` is annotated with the CAM-69 divergence marker on the same row as the filename. [oracle: file-assert: grep -qE 'check-agent-frontmatter\.ts.*CAM-69' vendor/README.md]
userStories.notes: Files: vendor/check-agent-frontmatter.ts (rewrite), src/vendor/_generated.ts (regenerate via `bun run embed-vendor`, do NOT hand-edit), vendor/README.md (annotate the check-agent-frontmatter.ts row with `CAM-69` on the SAME line as the filename so the F-04 oracle matches). Parser scope: top-level `key: scalar` pairs (string/number/bool) + simple block-sequence lists for `tools:` / `disallowedTools:` (lines matching `^  - <item>$` directly under the key). The agent frontmatter is intentionally simple; do NOT implement a full YAML parser. Reject unknown structural shapes with a line-numbered diagnostic so malformed agent files still get a useful message. Preserve the gcc-style format and the `closeLine` fallback for non-source-line violations. IMPORTANT (F-05 correction): vendor/ and claude-code-harness/ are EXCLUDED from tsconfig.json by design (see project CLAUDE.md `Quality Gates` section). Therefore `bun run typecheck` will NOT catch type errors in the rewritten parser. Correctness rests on `bun test` — specifically the two test/init.test.ts cases (`writes config.toml with permission_mode=bypassPermissions on a fresh path` and `preserves existing keys when re-running`, which exercise the smoke through `cam init`) returning to green, plus the US-002 standalone test. Defensive `T | undefined` guards are still required as code hygiene (the project standard is `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` everywhere, even outside the typecheck'd tree, so future authors don't trip on the same patterns). Keep all `node:` built-in imports (`node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:process`); only the bare `js-yaml` import is removed. After editing, run `bun run embed-vendor` then `bun run embed-vendor:check` and finally `bun test test/embedded.test.ts` to confirm parity. The vendor source's header comment currently references `docs/runbooks/cam-loop-recovery.md` (stale, pre-existing); the implementer MAY update that comment to `docs/recovery-runbook.md` in passing but it is NOT a required AC (F-06 scope decision). Skills: vendor-embed conventions in vendor/README.md and scripts/generate-embedded-vendor.ts. Patterns to re-check: scripts/cam/patterns.md `Bun runtime`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `No em-dash in persisted .md`. Lesson: comments don't prove behavior, run the smoke under a real tmpdir to confirm zero-dep (covered by US-002).

userStories.title: Deterministic regression test for the zero-dep smoke
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a deterministic regression test that proves the smoke runs cleanly in a tmpdir with no node_modules and no Bun auto-install, so the original `Missing default export` failure shape cannot silently come back.
acceptanceCriteria: The new standalone test file test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts materializes a fresh tmpdir (via mkdtemp), runs `git init` in it, writes a minimal `.claude/agents/` fixture, and invokes the smoke via spawnSync (Bun.spawnSync or node:child_process spawnSync) with `bun` + the script path. It must NOT shell out to `bun install` or `bun add`. [oracle: file-assert: grep -q mkdtemp test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts && grep -q 'git init' test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts && grep -qE 'spawnSync|Bun\.spawnSync' test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts && grep -q "'bun'" test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts && ! grep -qE 'bun install|bun add' test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts]
The test asserts the smoke exits 0 and stdout contains `agent file(s) ok`. [oracle: file-assert: grep -q 'agent file(s) ok' test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts]

The test passes even when Bun's install cache is empty/throwaway — i.e. any accidental auto-install would fail offline-equivalent and surface as a test failure. This is the core CAM-69 invariant (the smoke never reaches an auto-install code path). [oracle: named-command: BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)" bun test test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts]

Cache-state independence sanity (secondary): the smoke does not depend on the operator's global Bun cache state (passes whether the cache has js-yaml@5, js-yaml@4, or neither). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The two previously-failing init tests pass on the same green run: `writes config.toml with permission_mode=bypassPermissions on a fresh path` and `preserves existing keys when re-running`. [oracle: named-command: bun test test/init.test.ts -t 'writes config.toml with permission_mode=bypassPermissions on a fresh path']
Second pinned init test passes. [oracle: named-command: bun test test/init.test.ts -t 'preserves existing keys when re-running']
The new standalone test passes. [oracle: named-command: bun test test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: named-command: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass. [oracle: named-command: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: test/vendor/check-agent-frontmatter-standalone.test.ts (new). The materialization path must mirror src/commands/init.ts:runVendoredSmoke (writeFileSync of the embedded constant — import from src/vendor/_generated.ts — to a tmpdir path, then spawnSync('bun', [scriptPath])). Include a minimal `.claude/agents/example.md` fixture with valid frontmatter (name/description/model + one of tools/disallowedTools) and run `git init` in the tmpdir (the smoke uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). Use Bun.spawnSync or node:child_process spawnSync; do NOT shell out to `bun install`. Cleanup the tmpdir in afterEach. The F-02 named-command oracle (BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=tmp) is the load-bearing check: it forces any accidental auto-install to fail by pointing Bun at an empty cache, so if the parser still imports js-yaml the test fails offline-equivalent. Patterns to re-check: scripts/cam/patterns.md `Bun runtime` (prefer Bun.spawn over node:child_process where feasible, but matching runVendoredSmoke uses spawnSync — either is acceptable as long as it does not run install).

userStories.title: Defensive hardening of in-repo js-yaml default import + runbook note
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need every in-repo `js-yaml` consumer to use the v4/v5-compatible named import so a future js-yaml@5 bump does not break `cam status`, and the recovery runbook must mention the CAM-69 fix so an operator hitting a stale binary knows the diagnostic path.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/status.ts no longer uses `import yaml from 'js-yaml'`; it uses a named import (e.g. `import { load } from 'js-yaml'`) and call sites are adjusted accordingly. [oracle: file-assert: ! grep -q "^import yaml from 'js-yaml'" src/commands/status.ts && grep -q "from 'js-yaml'" src/commands/status.ts]

Any other `src/**` file that did `import yaml from 'js-yaml'` is switched to the named-import form (zero remaining default imports of js-yaml in src/). [oracle: file-assert: ! grep -RnE "^import yaml from 'js-yaml'" src/]

docs/recovery-runbook.md is updated with a CAM-69 section noting the zero-dep smoke fix and the rebuild/reinstall step required to clear a stale-binary `Missing default export` failure. [oracle: file-assert: grep -q 'CAM-69' docs/recovery-runbook.md]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: named-command: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass. [oracle: named-command: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/status.ts (named-import refactor + adjust `yaml.load(...)` -> `load(...)` call sites), grep src/ for any other default `js-yaml` import and fix in the same edit (likely only status.ts but verify), docs/recovery-runbook.md (append a CAM-69 section — F-06 operator decision: use the EXISTING docs/recovery-runbook.md, do NOT create a parallel docs/runbooks/cam-loop-recovery.md). The section must explain the zero-dep smoke fix and the rebuild/reinstall step (`bun run build:release --install` or equivalent) so an operator hitting `Missing default export` knows to clear a stale binary. Patterns: scripts/cam/patterns.md `No em-dash in persisted .md` applies to the doc edit. The js-yaml@4 pin in package.json means status.ts works today regardless, but a transitive `bun update` could float to v5 and break it silently; the named import is forward-compatible per the v4/v5 docs (load() exists in both).
